decision: Build one private Products and Investigate claims pull request, then test three products
why: The user authorized unattended implementation and one coherent vertical slice keeps product behavior reviewable

decision: Treat every structured external service as a Product; arbitrary transcript mentions do not create records
why: Products must unify Scout accounts and experiment targets without allowing chat text to pollute the registry

decision: Use Firecrawl Agent as the first production baseline and compare a Convex Agent approach in Lab
why: Firecrawl already supports autonomous URL discovery, structured schemas, async jobs, traces, and credit caps

decision: Use additive Product references with a bounded idempotent in-app sync for existing structured domains
why: Existing production rows cannot gain a required reference in one deploy, and page-triggered admin sync avoids a hidden manual production migration

decision: Use Firecrawl spark-2 with explicit credit and polling limits while preserving the previous completed result on refresh failure
why: Spark 1 names are deprecated and an investigation refresh must not erase already useful evidence

decision: Select Otio as the third live investigation target
why: It has ambitious first-party claims, free observable entry, and a concrete qualification tension without requiring personal or production assets

decision: Raise the Firecrawl Agent ceiling to 150 credits and capture qualifiers and tensions
why: Independent research found 30 credits likely to fail ordinary Agent discovery and claim qualifications are central to the product outcome

decision: Move the account-to-experiment backfill phase boundary into a scheduled continuation
why: Browser QA showed Convex rejects two paginated queries in one mutation even though the backend typechecked

decision: Reject the direct Firecrawl Agent baseline pending redesign
why: Samebase remained processing for 90 bounded polls and timed out at 15 minutes; Tally and Otio were not started to avoid multiplying an unvalidated cost/latency contract

decision: Treat the Samebase timeout as a provider-contract defect rather than transient flakiness
why: The request supplied only the homepage while strict URL confinement forbade the Agent from opening the pricing, docs, security, and integration pages demanded by the prompt; the remote job later reported failed

decision: Replace new direct Agent jobs with bounded Map, optional Search, first-party Scrape, and one Convex Agent synthesis
why: The deterministic path caps retrieval near nine Firecrawl credits, exposes exact evidence pages, prevents invented citations through opaque source IDs, and should finish in roughly one to two minutes while retaining the same product workflow

decision: Retain the legacy Firecrawl Agent schema family and start only the new Firecrawl plus Convex family
why: The failed development row must remain readable across schema deployment while Retry can create a truthful new provider record

decision: Accept bounded Firecrawl retrieval and reject Convex Gateway structured output as the synthesis transport
why: Samebase mapped and scraped first-party pages in about 24 seconds at a conservative seven-credit count, then even a minimal Luna generateObject smoke returned HTTP 400 while the same model's generateText smoke succeeded
evidence: live Products UI; Convex logs; temporary structured-output diagnostic

decision: Use one plain Convex Agent generateText call with a strict bounded JSON parser
why: This preserves the fresh traceable Luna thread and one-call budget while avoiding the gateway's unsupported structured-output path; Zod and opaque source hydration remain the trusted boundary

decision: Accept the bounded retrieval plus JSON-text synthesis pipeline for Samebase and Tally
why: Both products completed in roughly 20-30 seconds at seven conservatively counted Firecrawl credits with first-party source links, qualifications, tensions, unknowns, and suggested mystery shops
evidence: live Products UI; productInvestigations; Agent component traces

decision: Normalize harmless model list overproduction before retrying Otio
why: Otio returned otherwise valid JSON with 10 claims, seven dependencies, one tension, and eight unknowns, but six audiences exceeded the five-item public cap; invalid evidence and citations must remain hard failures
evidence: live Products UI; Agent component message summary

decision: Accept the complete three-product vertical slice
why: Samebase, Tally, and Otio all completed with seven conservatively counted Firecrawl credits; expanded UI reports used five, four, and five actual first-party sources respectively and retained unverified-claim language
evidence: live Products UI; productInvestigations; Agent component traces

decision: Use Otio's surfaced quota and OCR tensions as proof that investigation can shape later mystery shops
why: The report contrasted no-file-cap language with explicit upload/storage quotas and identified unclear ownership between an Otio OCR service and Datalab

decision: Accept both P3 findings from the independent cross-model review
why: The UI had one stale registry-cap string and could call a scheduled paginated import complete before every page landed

decision: Let the authenticated Products page drain and await each bounded legacy-sync cursor
why: One Convex mutation still performs only one paginated query, while the UI now knows exactly when the registry is complete and can report failure truthfully
